chunks: And Isma'il ibn Abi Fudayk narrated from Abu 'Abdillah, from his father, peace be upon them both, who said:
Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Exalted, is with the debtor until he repays it, so long as he did not take it from that which is forbidden to him.

key_terms.إِنَّ: Indeed; a particle of emphasis introducing the statement
key_terms.صَاحِبِ الدَّيْنِ: the debtor; the one burdened with debt
key_terms.يَأْخُذْهُ: he takes it; he acquires it
key_terms.يَحْرُمُ: is forbidden; is haram for him
key_terms.يُؤَدِّيَهُ: he repays it; he fulfills the debt owed

ai.seo_question: Is Allah with a person who is in debt?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that Allah’s support remains with a debtor who is seeking to fulfill his obligation and repay what he owes. It also sets an ethical limit: this divine support applies so long as the debt was not taken or pursued through what is haram (forbidden).

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3692 - Isma'il ibn Abi Fudayk narrated from Abu Abdillah Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) from his father, Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as), who said:
"Indeed, Allah (swt), the Mighty and Exalted, is with the debtor until he repays his debt, as long as he did not acquire it through what is forbidden to him."
